_metadata.rubric: x03 rubric (x02 bar + five content questions + already_served context), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and the single input file x03-v-review-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: AFRICA via the classic wildlife safari, WEB via Apple's Safari browser; a clean double meaning that matches the owner-approved INTERNET + AFRICA example.

pairs.pair_note: Ideal pair for SAFARI; both sides are direct.

hints.reason: ANTARCTICA via the frozen continent, COMPUTER via a frozen (unresponsive) machine; the same double meaning as the owner-approved STATUE + COMPUTER.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; FROZEN is reused across many COMPUTER pairs in this batch, which matters only if two such targets share a board.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the Baltimore Orioles, BIRD via the orange-and-black songbird; a fair team-name double meaning on par with the served CARDINAL and JAY.

pairs.pair_note: CARDINAL (already served) is slightly more universal, but ORIOLE is an equally fair alternative and both can stand.

hints.reason: BLACK and WHITE are the two sides in chess, and the line's 'white moves first' is accurate; fair and quick, if not a big surprise.

pairs.pair_note: Many hints fit this pair (ZEBRA, PANDA, PIANO, OREO); none is clearly better than CHESS, though ZEBRA or PANDA might feel more playful.

hints.reason: BOARD via the chessboard, HORSE via the horse-headed knight; the knight step gives a nice small click.

pairs.pair_note: Good use of CHESS; the HORSE side is the satisfying part.

hints.reason: CHAIR via the beanbag chair, FOOD via the 'bean' inside the word; the owner approved the same idea for FOOD + COUCH, and CHAIR is an even tighter fit.

pairs.pair_note: The FOOD side relies on spotting 'bean' in the word, which is the intended charm.

hints.reason: CHECK via putting the king in check, KING via the chess piece you must protect; accurate and instant.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean.

hints.reason: CLOWN via Ronald McDonald, HAMBURGER via McDonald's burgers; a brand written as one word, fair to a U.S. audience.

pairs.pair_note: RONALD (already served) leans on CLOWN, MCDONALDS leans on HAMBURGER; both are good and neither is clearly better.

hints.reason: COLD via freezing temperatures, COMPUTER via a frozen screen; close to COLD but not a plain synonym, so it stays fair.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; the COLD side is very direct.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via a frozen machine, FROST via frozen ice crystals; accurate and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Standard FROZEN double meaning.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via a frozen machine, PENGUIN via icy Antarctic habitat; the penguin side is one step removed but penguins and ice are a strong popular association.
hints.fix: A frozen computer stops responding, and many penguins live in frozen Antarctica.

pairs.pair_note: Explanation implies all penguins live in Antarctica (the line already says 'many'). LINUX (Tux the penguin mascot) is a cleverer route but too niche to count as clearly better.

hints.reason: RAIN falls from clouds, COMPUTER files are backed up to the cloud; a crisp, familiar double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and satisfying.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via a frozen machine, SNOW as frozen water; accurate and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Standard FROZEN double meaning; the Disney film (Olaf, snow) adds a little extra pull.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via a frozen machine, WINTER via frozen weather; fair, though the explanation overstates lakes freezing 'solid'.
hints.fix: A frozen computer stops responding, and winter freezes lakes and ponds over.

pairs.pair_note: Lakes and ponds usually freeze only on the surface; drop 'solid'.

hints.reason: Both COOKIE and MILK come together in the familiar scene of dunking a cookie in milk; slightly more vivid than the served DIP.
COOKIE because an Oreo is the iconic cookie, MILK through the twist-lick-dunk ritual and 'Milk's favorite cookie' branding; a specific, pleasing reference rather than a synonym.

pairs.pair_note: Both new hints beat or match the served DIP; OREO has the most character.

hints.reason: DESERT via sand dunes, WORM via the giant sandworms of Dune; works as plain word and as pop culture at once, with accurate text.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; recent films make the WORM side broadly known.

hints.reason: DINOSAUR via T. rex, KING via rex being Latin for king; the 'tyrant lizard king' translation is correct and gives a real 'oh, nice'.

pairs.pair_note: Best home for REX in this batch.

hints.reason: DISEASE via scurvy itself (vitamin C deficiency, correctly stated), PIRATE via sailors on long voyages and the pirate-speak 'scurvy dog'.

pairs.pair_note: Strongest of the three SCURVY pairs; the 'ye scurvy dog' echo adds fun.

hints.reason: DISNEY via the hit film Frozen, ICE via frozen water and Elsa's ice powers; both sides land at once.

pairs.pair_note: Very good use of FROZEN.

hints.reason: DOLL and FASHION both point straight at Barbie, the famous fashion doll; easy but exactly right.

pairs.pair_note: An obvious, excellent hint.

hints.reason: DOLL via Barbie the doll, PINK via 'Barbie pink' and the 2023 film's pink everything; slightly more fun than DOLL + FASHION.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, culturally fresh link.

hints.reason: ICE via frozen water and Elsa's powers, MOVIE via the Disney film; fair, though MOVIE is a broad target.

pairs.pair_note: Good; DISNEY + ICE is the tighter version of the same idea.

hints.reason: WEB via the Safari browser is solid, but JUNGLE is weak because safaris are savanna trips (the line has to fall back on 'a trip into the wild'), and AMAZON (rainforest + the website) hits both sides squarely.

pairs.pair_note: Use AMAZON for this pair; keep SAFARI for AFRICA + WEB.

hints.reason: TOY via Toy Story's Rex is instant; KING via Latin rex is less immediate but widely known through T. rex and Oedipus Rex, and it clicks on explanation.

pairs.pair_note: Weaker than DINOSAUR + KING or the owner's TOY + DINOSAUR, since KING needs the Latin step; close to the BORDERLINE line.

hints.reason: LEAD via the lead-into-gold quest, SCIENCE via alchemy as chemistry's forerunner (accurately framed); mirrors the owner-approved GOLD + SCIENCE.

pairs.pair_note: Good; LEAD is arguably a more pleasing target than GOLD since it is the less obvious half.

hints.reason: LEMON via citrus juice given to sailors against scurvy (historically accurate), PIRATE via long voyages and 'scurvy dog'; a satisfying fact link.

pairs.pair_note: Nice: neither target names a disease, so the hint feels discovered.

hints.reason: MOVIE via the Disney film, SNOWMAN via Olaf; also reads literally as a frozen snowman.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; Olaf makes it delightful.

hints.reason: OCEAN via submarines travelling underwater, YELLOW via the Beatles' Yellow Submarine; a well-known song that gives a real click.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; older but still universally known reference.

hints.reason: ORANGE via the vitamin C that prevents scurvy, PIRATE via long voyages; accurate and fair, slightly less vivid than LEMON since the naval history is about lemons and limes.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; LEMON + PIRATE is the cleaner version.

hints.reason: TOY via Toy Story's Hamm, PIG via the piggy bank and the 'ham' pun in his name; works even for players who half-remember the film.

pairs.pair_note: Nice two-layer hint (character plus pun).

hints.reason: POTATO via 'Potato Head' is instant, but TOY is reached only by already completing that same phrase; HEAD on its own does not suggest TOY and fits many board words.

pairs.pair_note: The single-phrase blank makes this flat; no obvious one-word replacement stands out, so it may simply be a weak pair.

hints.reason: RAIN falls from clouds, WEB services store files in the cloud; fair, a touch looser than COMPUTER + RAIN.

pairs.pair_note: Good; COMPUTER + RAIN is the tighter home for CLOUD.

hints.reason: TOY via Buzz Lightyear, SPACE via his space-ranger role (and astronaut Buzz Aldrin as a bonus route); instant and fun.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; two independent routes to SPACE.
